text: Drought. "Not a cloud in months. The locusts, at least, are having a fine year." Every province collects an average harvest. The population holds at one hundred million, times one, so everyone reads the first row of their table. No disasters are named, so nobody turns a page in their booklet. An ordinary year. I'll remind you that the crown has kept its word in ordinary years before.

Paid out to the grain, friends: fifteen to Her Majesty, thirty-five to Clark, Silke and Paddy, fifty-five to the Gentry's humble granary, and ten to Rob. And the rent stays the customary five, a dry year being no excuse for a thirsty landlord. Paddy, I hope that buys the Gentry a little goodwill on the coast. Her Majesty has kept her word in ordinary years, and so has the Gentry.
Rich pays out the harvest: Reina +15, Clark, Silke and Paddy +35 each, Rich +55 (the Reservoir's +20), Rob +10. He asks the minimum rent; Silke and Paddy pay him 5 each.

Fifty again: the fifth year running, and you can set your calendars by it. In return the crown digs the first section of the Grand Canal through Province 6, at the crown's own cost. Paddy, you gave me a year out loud. Here's what I give you for it, and it'll still be paying you ten a harvest long after this drought is forgotten. Clark keeps his fifteen.

Reina declares 50% for the fifth year: 17.5 each from Clark, Silke and Paddy, 27.5 from Rich, 5 from Rob (who refuses his). The crown digs the first section of the Province 6 Grand Canal, all 40 from the reserve (+10 to Paddy's harvest from next year), and pays Clark 15 at the year's end.

Seventeen and a half, paid, counted twice and written down once. Five years at fifty percent, Majesty: page one of the book now just says "consistently". But a canal is a canal, and the crown's collector doesn't burn the house down the year it finally builds something. Paddy, enjoy your ten a harvest. Rob, your refusal goes on the usual page.

Twenty-seven and a half, Your Majesty, and gladly. A canal on the coast, the tax steady five years running: that is a crown worth paying. I'll only note, for Clark's book, that the Gentry pays in full every year while some among us don't pay at all.

Fifty percent, five years running. That puts me at a hundred grain to the crown with this year's seventeen and a half, and Her Majesty is sitting on three hundred and fifty-six. Lovely canal, Paddy, truly, it'll pay you ten a year. Nothing's being dug on my coast. If anyone calls this tax what it is, I'm standing behind them, and I'll have my soldier with me.

Seventeen and a half, and I'll hand it over without the face I usually make. I said if nothing got built south of Silke's beach I'd call the cause, and something has. A canal's the sort of promise you can stand in up to your knees, so I'll call it kept. Rich, the rent's paid and the goodwill's started. Don't spend it all at once.
Reina's built in the south, so I won't call it this year. If the crown stops building, or starts squeezing the coast again, you'll find me beside you the same as before.

Five, Clark? I'll keep it, thank you, same as every year. And Your Majesty's quite right, you could set a calendar by it: half of everything, five years running, through a drought, with the locusts eating better than Silke does. If that isn't 'consistently excessive' I don't know what the words are for. I'm calling it. Paddy, I know you've just been handed a very nice ditch, but one canal doesn't make fifty percent any smaller. Silke, you know where to sign.

Clark, Rich and Paddy will pay. Rob refuses his 5 and calls a revolt on 'taxes are consistently excessive'; Silke backs it. One more agreeing is needed. The answers crossed, so Clark, Rich and Paddy are each asked once whether they agree.

Rob, the cause is in my book, five years of it, dated and underlined twice. Written down is one thing, though, and called by a man who won't pay his five is another. The collector doesn't sign a revolt for a taxpayer who never pays. That's a no from me, and it goes on your page under "cheek, again".

Your Majesty, it pains me, but five years at half of everything is "consistently", and Clark has the book to prove it. So the Gentry agrees the cause exists. My price is posted, the same way as always: hand back my twenty-seven and a half and ten more for the trouble, and I take it back the moment it's paid, every grain, as I have twice before.

Rob, I gave Her Majesty a year, out loud. She spent it digging a canal through my fields, and I'm not going to stand in the wet and say she did nothing. Fifty's a heavy load, Silke, I know it, and I'll say so the day the building stops. But I won't help Rob pull the roof down the same week they've fixed the gutter.

I'm not backing out on you, I'm keeping a promise I made in front of everyone. Get the crown to say out loud it will build on your coast next, and if it doesn't, you'll have my name on the next call. Make it your call, not Rob's.

Clark and Paddy don't agree. Rich agrees, with his price posted: his 27.5 back and 10 more. With Silke and Rich agreeing, Rob's revolt is called, and play stops until it stands or is dropped. Reina may answer.

A rule worth stating: if a revolt stands, the throne goes only by acclamation, and only claimants are counted, each on their own grain in hand, the soldiers they control and their friends (backers). Reina, deposed, couldn't claim, and the sealed reserve would pass whole to whoever is acclaimed. A claimant must lead two of the three counts, so Rob, with one soldier and no friends yet, couldn't be acclaimed without backers. A revolt crowns whoever the table backs.

The rate stands at fifty. I won't haggle over it in front of a man who's never paid a grain of it. Rich, here's your price, counted out in front of everyone so nobody can say the Gentry's loyalty comes cheap. And Silke, so you know I heard you: next year the crown digs the first canal section through Province 5, at the crown's own cost. The coast gets water on both sides.

Reina answers: she pays Rich 37.5 from the reserve (his posted price), keeps the rate at 50%, and promises the first Province 5 Grand Canal section next year, all 40 from the crown. Rob, Silke and Rich now each stand by the revolt or take it back.

I'm standing by it. Rich, that's three times now, and you've earned thirty-seven and a half for holding a pen. Next spring I'll call it again just to see what your price has gone up to. Silke, a canal promised for next year is still just a promise, but you have the coast to think of, so do what you have to. Majesty, I'll say this much: you've a very good accountant in Rich.

A canal through Province 5 next year, at the crown's cost, said out loud in front of six people. Majesty, I'll take that over Rob's empty chair, and I'm taking it back. But Rich just got thirty-seven and a half for the third time and I got a promise, so I'll be counting shovels. If there's no water on my coast by next harvest, the next call is mine, and I won't be calling it alone.
You heard her promise it. If the Province 5 canal isn't dug next year, I'm calling it, and I'm holding you to that name on the call.

Thirty-seven and a half, counted out where everyone could see it. The Gentry's price was posted, paid and honoured, so I take it back, every grain. And Silke, a canal on your coast next year is a better answer than any revolt would have given you.

Silke and Rich take it back; Rob stands alone, so the revolt is dropped and play resumes. Clark collects the 50%: 17.5 each from Clark, Silke and Paddy and 27.5 from Rich (Rob refuses his 5). Reina digs the first section of the Province 6 Grand Canal for 40 (+10 to Paddy's harvest from next year). Nothing is for sale, so there are no auctions.

Rich, you've been paid three times this year for being loyal, so I'm sure you won't miss a bowl. It's on M15 now, in my desert, if you'd like to come and look at it. And because I'm a generous man I've hired a lad on N12 to keep an eye on your Dragon Jar for you. Nobody at this table told me to do any of that, Majesty. I did it all myself.

Rob marches W1 onto L14 and takes Rich's Wooden Bowl instead of the 5, setting it on M15 in the desert: his first piece, and Rich's set is broken (he holds the Customs House and Dragon Jar; Province 3 is now raided, so soldiers Rich buys can move). Rob hires a second soldier on N12, beside Rich's Jar on M12 (army 2 of 3). Reina pays Clark 15.

End of Year 5. Grain: Reina (the reserve) 343.5, Clark 116, Rich 203.5, Silke 72, Paddy 83, Rob 92. Soldiers: Rob's W1 on L14 and W2 on N12; Clark's on I14; Silke's on Q24. One complete set: Clark's. Built: both palaces, the Province 3 Reservoir, one section of the Province 6 canal. Reina has promised the first Province 5 canal section next year. Works still owed: 730. Year 6's card is drawn next.
